usage_note: Points to what you're talking about. Written は but said 'wa' as a particle.
example_japanese: 私は アメリカ人 です。

usage_note: Marks WHO is doing the action. Used for emphasis or introducing something new.
example_japanese: 神様が あなたを 愛しています。

usage_note: Marks the thing receiving the action — what is being read, loved, or eaten.
example_japanese: 聖書を 読みます。

usage_note: Connects two nouns. The first one owns the second. 私の = my.
example_japanese: 私の 名前は ジョンです。

usage_note: Shows direction or location. Points toward where you're going or where something is.
example_japanese: 教会に 来てください。

english: Where action happens / By means of
usage_note: Shows WHERE something takes place, or the tool/method used to do it.
example_japanese: バスで 行きます。

usage_note: Connects nouns together, or means 'together with' a person.
example_japanese: 友達と 教会に 行きます。
example_english: I'll go to church with a friend.

usage_note: Replaces は or が to say 'also.' Great for agreeing or including yourself.
example_japanese: 私も クリスチャン です。

usage_note: Add か to the END of any sentence to make it a question. No word order change needed!
example_japanese: 教会に 来ますか？

usage_note: Added to the end to seek agreement or soften a statement. Very friendly and common.
example_japanese: いい天気 ですね。

usage_note: After a place = 'from.' You will say アメリカから every single day on this trip.
example_japanese: アメリカから 来ました。

usage_note: Shows an endpoint in space or time. 駅まで = up to the station.
example_japanese: 駅まで 行きたいです。
example_english: I want to go to the station.

usage_note: The polite 'to be.' Ends almost every sentence. Makes you sound respectful.
example_japanese: 私は クリスチャン です。

usage_note: Attaches to a verb to make it polite. 行きます = I go. 食べます = I eat.
example_japanese: 毎日 祈ります。

usage_note: Negative version of ます. 行きません = I don't go. 食べません = I don't eat.
example_japanese: 肉を 食べません。

usage_note: Past tense of ます. Swap ます → ました. 来ました = I came. 食べました = I ate.
example_japanese: アメリカから 来ました。

usage_note: Attach to a verb to make a polite request. ゆっくり話してください = please speak slowly.
example_japanese: ゆっくり 話してください。

usage_note: The first three numbers. に also means 'two' — same sound as the particle に, don't confuse them!
example_japanese: 三人 います。

usage_note: The first three numbers. に also means 'two' — same sound as the particle に, don't confuse them!
example_japanese: 三人 います。

usage_note: The first three numbers. に also means 'two' — same sound as the particle に, don't confuse them!
example_japanese: 三人 います。

usage_note: Four has two readings: し (shi) or よん (yon). よん is more common in conversation.
example_japanese: 五時に 来てください。

usage_note: Four has two readings: し (shi) or よん (yon). よん is more common in conversation.
example_japanese: 五時に 来てください。

usage_note: Four has two readings: し (shi) or よん (yon). よん is more common in conversation.
example_japanese: 五時に 来てください。

usage_note: Seven = しち or なな. Nine = く or きゅう. Both readings are used — context tells you which.
example_japanese: 九時に 礼拝が 始まります。
example_english: The service starts at nine o'clock.

usage_note: Seven = しち or なな. Nine = く or きゅう. Both readings are used — context tells you which.
example_japanese: 九時に 礼拝が 始まります。
example_english: The service starts at nine o'clock.

usage_note: Seven = しち or なな. Nine = く or きゅう. Both readings are used — context tells you which.
example_japanese: 九時に 礼拝が 始まります。
example_english: The service starts at nine o'clock.

usage_note: 十 = 10. 十一 = 11. 二十 = 20. 百 = 100. 千 = 1,000. Stack numbers to make bigger ones.
example_japanese: 千円 です。

usage_note: 十 = 10. 十一 = 11. 二十 = 20. 百 = 100. 千 = 1,000. Stack numbers to make bigger ones.
example_japanese: 千円 です。

usage_note: 十 = 10. 十一 = 11. 二十 = 20. 百 = 100. 千 = 1,000. Stack numbers to make bigger ones.
example_japanese: 千円 です。

usage_note: Use with anyone you don't know well. With close friends, おはよう alone is fine.
example_japanese: おはようございます！今日も よい一日を。
example_english: Good morning! Have a great day today too.
literal_breakdown: Good morning! Today also → good day [have].

usage_note: The standard daytime greeting. Safe to use with absolutely anyone.
example_japanese: こんにちは！はじめまして。

usage_note: Used after the sun goes down. Same politeness as こんにちは.
example_japanese: こんばんは！礼拝は どうでしたか？
example_english: Good evening! How was the service?

usage_note: Said when someone is going to sleep or leaving for the night. Not a general goodbye.
example_japanese: おやすみなさい。また明日！

usage_note: Carries a sense of finality — like you won't see them for a long time. Use またね for casual.
example_japanese: さようなら。また来年 会いましょう。
example_english: Goodbye. Let's meet again next year.
literal_breakdown: Goodbye. Again next year → let's meet.

usage_note: Casual goodbye used with people you know.
example_japanese: じゃあね！連絡してね。

english: See you later / bye for now
usage_note: Friendly warm goodbye; better than さようなら for casual follow-up.
example_japanese: じゃあね！連絡してね。

english: Nice to meet you (first meeting only)
usage_note: ONLY for the very first time you meet someone. Always follow with よろしくお願いします.
example_japanese: はじめまして。ジョンです。よろしく！
example_english: Nice to meet you. I'm Jon. Pleased to meet you!
literal_breakdown: First meeting. Jon → am. Please treat me well!

japanese: よろしくお願いします
english: Pleased to meet you / Please be kind to me
usage_note: No perfect English translation. Closes a self-intro and expresses goodwill. Never skip it!
example_japanese: アメリカから来ました。よろしくお願いします。
example_english: I came from America. Pleased to meet you.
literal_breakdown: America [from] came. → Kindly please treat me.

japanese: ありがとうございます
usage_note: The full polite thank you. Use with anyone you want to show respect.
example_japanese: 助けてくれて ありがとうございます。

usage_note: Formal response to ありがとう. In casual settings, 大丈夫 or いいえ also work.
example_japanese: ありがとう！— どういたしまして。

usage_note: Gets someone's attention OR lightly apologizes. One of the most-used words on any Japan trip!
example_japanese: すみません、トイレは どこですか？
example_english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

usage_note: Stronger than すみません. Use when you've actually done something wrong.
example_japanese: 遅れて ごめんなさい。

english: It's okay / I'm fine / No problem
usage_note: Very versatile. Can mean 'I'm fine,' 'no worries,' or even 'no thank you' depending on context.
example_japanese: 大丈夫ですか？— はい、大丈夫です。
example_english: Are you okay? — Yes, I'm fine.
literal_breakdown: Okay are you? → Yes, okay am.

usage_note: Polite yes.
example_japanese: 教会に来ますか？— はい、行きます。
example_english: Will you come to church? — Yes, I will.

usage_note: Polite no.
example_japanese: 教会に来ますか？— はい、行きます。
example_english: Will you come to church? — Yes, I will.

usage_note: わかります = I understand. わかりません = I don't understand. You'll use both constantly.
example_japanese: 少し わかります。でも、ゆっくり 話してください。
example_english: I understand a little. But please speak slowly.
literal_breakdown: A little → understand. But, slowly → please speak.

japanese: もう一度お願いします
usage_note: Literally 'one more time, please.' Never be embarrassed to use this — people will appreciate it.
example_japanese: すみません、もう一度 お願いします。
example_english: Excuse me, please say that again.
literal_breakdown: Excuse me, one more time → please.

japanese: 日本語が少しわかります
usage_note: 少し = a little. Humble and honest. Sets good expectations and earns instant goodwill.
example_japanese: 日本語が少しわかります。英語を 話せますか？
example_english: I understand a little Japanese. Do you speak English?
literal_breakdown: Japanese [subject] a little understand. English [object] → speak can?

usage_note: お元気 = your wellbeing (お makes it polite). A warm, caring way to greet someone.
example_japanese: お元気ですか？— はい、元気です！
example_english: How are you? — Yes, I'm well!
literal_breakdown: Well are you? → Yes, well am!

usage_note: One of the most natural filler phrases in Japanese. Shows you're listening and agreeing.
example_japanese: 日本は美しいですね。— そうですね！
example_english: Japan is beautiful, isn't it. — Yes, indeed!
literal_breakdown: Japan [topic] beautiful is, right? → That's right!

english: I see / Makes sense / Ah, I understand
usage_note: Said when something clicks. A very natural response when someone explains something to you.
example_japanese: このバスは 札幌駅に 行きます。— なるほど！
example_english: This bus goes to Sapporo Station. — Ah, I see!
literal_breakdown: This bus [topic] → Sapporo station [to] → goes. — I see!

usage_note: また = again. 会いましょう = let's meet. Warm and genuine — perfect for ending a good conversation.
example_japanese: また会いましょう。連絡してください。
example_english: Let's meet again. Please keep in touch.
literal_breakdown: Again → let's meet. Contact → please do.

japanese: はじめまして。アメリカの教会から来ました。よろしくお願いします。
romaji: hajimemashite. amerika no kyoukai kara kimashita. yoroshiku onegaishimasu.
usage_note: This is your opening. Say it every single time you meet someone new. Own it completely.
example_japanese: はじめまして。アメリカの教会から来ました。よろしくお願いします。
example_english: Nice to meet you. I came from a church in America. Pleased to meet you.
literal_breakdown: First meeting. America's church [from] came. Kindly please treat me.

japanese: またお話しできますか？
usage_note: また = again. お話し = conversation (polite). できますか？ = can we/is it possible?
example_japanese: またお話し できますか？

japanese: 連絡先を交換しませんか？
english: Would you like to exchange contact info?
usage_note: 連絡先 = contact information. 交換する = to exchange. 〜しませんか？ = wouldn't you like to?
example_japanese: 連絡先を 交換しませんか？
example_english: Would you like to exchange contact info?
literal_breakdown: Contact info [object] → wouldn't you like to exchange?

usage_note: The city where you'll be. 札幌駅 = Sapporo Station. 大通り = Odori (main street area).
example_japanese: 札幌は 美しい街 です。

romaji: ___ yuki no basu wa doko desu ka?
english: Where is the bus going to ___?
usage_note: ___行き = bound for ___. の = possessive. Just fill in your destination before 行き.
example_japanese: 教会行きのバスは どこですか？
example_english: Where is the bus going to the church?

japanese: 乗り換えが必要ですか？
usage_note: 乗り換え = transfer (switching vehicles). 必要 = necessary/needed. Good to ask bus drivers.
example_japanese: 乗り換えが 必要ですか？

usage_note: 何番 = what number. 線 = line/track. Ask this at stations to find the right platform.
example_japanese: 札幌行きは 何番線ですか？

usage_note: 時刻 = time. 表 = chart/table. A bus or train schedule. Very useful for planning.
example_japanese: バスの時刻表は ありますか？

usage_note: 助ける = to help/rescue. 〜てください = please do. Say this clearly if you are in trouble.
example_japanese: すみません、助けてください。迷ってしまいました。
example_english: Excuse me, please help me. I got lost.
literal_breakdown: Excuse me, please help. Lost [got accidentally].

usage_note: 地図 = map. あります = there is/exists. ありませんか = isn't there? Good at any info desk.
example_japanese: すみません、地図は ありますか？
example_english: Excuse me, is there a map?

usage_note: 家族 = family. います = there is (for people/animals). いません = there is not.
example_japanese: 家族は いますか？— はい、妻と子供が います。
example_english: Do you have family? — Yes, I have a wife and children.
literal_breakdown: Family [topic] → is there? → Yes, wife and children → are.

usage_note: 子供 = child/children. います = exists/are (for living things). A warm conversation starter.
example_japanese: 子供は いますか？— はい、三人 います。
example_english: Do you have children? — Yes, I have three.
literal_breakdown: Children [topic] → are there? → Yes, three → are.

usage_note: 仕事 = work/job. 何 = what. A natural question when getting to know someone.
example_japanese: 仕事は 何ですか？

usage_note: 趣味 = hobby/interest. 何 = what. Opens up fun and friendly conversation.
example_japanese: 趣味は 何ですか？— 写真を 撮ります。
example_english: What are your hobbies? — I take photos.

japanese: どこに住んでいますか？
usage_note: どこ = where. 住んでいます = am living (ongoing state). 〜ていますか = are you ___ing?
example_japanese: どこに 住んでいますか？— 札幌に 住んでいます。
example_english: Where do you live? — I live in Sapporo.

usage_note: 好き = like/fond of. ですか = polite question. A great way to invite someone to share.
example_japanese: 札幌は 好きですか？— はい、大好きです！
example_english: Do you like Sapporo? — Yes, I love it!

usage_note: 大好き = love very much (大 = big/great + 好き = like). Say this and watch faces light up.
example_japanese: 日本が 大好きです。また来たいです。
example_english: I love Japan. I want to come again.
literal_breakdown: Japan [subject] → love. Again → want to come.

usage_note: また = again. 来たい = want to come. 来たいです = want to come (polite). A warm farewell.
example_japanese: 日本が大好きです。また来たいです。
example_english: I love Japan. I want to come again.
literal_breakdown: Japan love. Again → want to come.

japanese: 一緒に食事しませんか？
english: Would you like to eat together?
usage_note: 一緒に = together. 食事 = meal. 〜しませんか？ = wouldn't you like to...? Warm invitation.
example_japanese: 一緒に 食事しませんか？
example_english: Would you like to eat together?
literal_breakdown: Together → meal wouldn't you like to have?

usage_note: 連絡する = to contact/reach out. 〜してください = please do. Say this at every goodbye.
example_japanese: またね。連絡してください。

japanese: また会いましょう。連絡してください。
english: The farewell that keeps the door open
usage_note: Again → let's meet. Contact → please do. Say this to everyone you want to see again.
example_japanese: また会いましょう。連絡してください。
example_english: Let's meet again. Please keep in touch.
literal_breakdown: Again → let's meet. Contact → please do.

usage_note: いくら = how much (money). ですか = polite question. Essential for any shopping.
example_japanese: これは いくらですか？

usage_note: Just say the number + 円 + です. No extra words needed. 五百円です = It's 500 yen.
example_japanese: 五百円 です。

usage_note: どこ = where. Put any place before it: 教会はどこですか？ = Where is the church?
example_japanese: トイレは どこですか？

usage_note: 右 = right. 左 = left. You'll use these when someone gives you directions.
example_japanese: 右に 曲がってください。

usage_note: 右 = right. 左 = left. You'll use these when someone gives you directions.
example_japanese: 右に 曲がってください。

usage_note: Used when giving or getting directions. まっすぐ行ってください = please go straight.
example_japanese: まっすぐ 行ってください。

usage_note: 近い = close/near. 遠い = far. Very useful for judging distances when navigating.
example_japanese: 駅は 近いですか？

usage_note: ここ = here (near me). そこ = there (near you). あそこ = over there (away from both of us).
example_japanese: 教会は あそこです。

usage_note: ここ = here (near me). そこ = there (near you). あそこ = over there (away from both of us).
example_japanese: 教会は あそこです。

usage_note: ここ = here (near me). そこ = there (near you). あそこ = over there (away from both of us).
example_japanese: 教会は あそこです。

usage_note: You'll see this kanji everywhere in Japan. 札幌駅 = Sapporo Station.
example_japanese: 札幌駅は どこですか？

usage_note: バス is from the English 'bus.' 電車 = electric train. You'll use both in Sapporo.
example_japanese: このバスは 教会に 行きますか？
example_english: Does this bus go to the church?

usage_note: バス is from the English 'bus.' 電車 = electric train. You'll use both in Sapporo.
example_japanese: このバスは 教会に 行きますか？
example_english: Does this bus go to the church?

usage_note: The word for a transit or entry ticket. 切符はどこで買えますか？ = Where can I buy a ticket?
example_japanese: 切符を ください。

usage_note: 出 = exit/leave. 入 = enter. 口 = mouth/opening. You'll see these signs everywhere.
example_japanese: 出口は どこですか？

usage_note: 出 = exit/leave. 入 = enter. 口 = mouth/opening. You'll see these signs everywhere.
example_japanese: 出口は どこですか？

usage_note: まで = up to. 行きたい = want to go. Fill in your destination. Very useful on buses.
example_japanese: 札幌駅まで 行きたいです。
example_english: I want to go to Sapporo Station.
literal_breakdown: Sapporo Station [up to] → want to go.

usage_note: 次 = next. 停留所 = bus stop. Ask the driver or another passenger if unsure.
example_japanese: 次の停留所は どこですか？

japanese: ここで降りてもいいですか？
romaji: koko de orite mo ii desu ka?
usage_note: 降りる = to get off. 〜てもいいですか = is it okay if I...? Very polite request.
example_japanese: ここで 降りてもいいですか？

usage_note: 〜てしまいました = something happened accidentally. Humble and natural-sounding.
example_japanese: すみません、迷ってしまいました。助けてください。
example_english: Excuse me, I got lost. Please help me.
literal_breakdown: Excuse me, got lost [accidentally]. Help → please.

usage_note: 歩いて = on foot/walking. 何分 = how many minutes. Great for judging whether to walk or ride.
example_japanese: 駅まで 歩いて何分ですか？
example_english: How many minutes on foot to the station?
literal_breakdown: Station [to] → walking how many minutes is?

japanese: タクシーを呼んでください
usage_note: タクシー = taxi (from English). 呼ぶ = to call/summon. 〜てください = please do.
example_japanese: すみません、タクシーを 呼んでください。
example_english: Excuse me, please call a taxi.

usage_note: メニュー = menu (from English). 〜をください = please give me ___. Simple and polite.
example_japanese: すみません、メニューを ください。
example_english: Excuse me, please give me a menu.

usage_note: The most useful restaurant phrase. Fill the blank with what you want. 水をください = water please.
example_japanese: 水を ください。

usage_note: おすすめ = recommendation. 何 = what. Great for connecting with locals over food.
example_japanese: おすすめは 何ですか？

usage_note: One word that will make every cook or host beam with joy. Say it with feeling!
example_japanese: これは おいしいです！

usage_note: 水 = water. お茶 = tea (お is a polite prefix). Both are usually free at Japanese restaurants.
example_japanese: お茶を ください。

usage_note: 水 = water. お茶 = tea (お is a polite prefix). Both are usually free at Japanese restaurants.
example_japanese: お茶を ください。

usage_note: ご飯 literally means rice but also means 'meal' in general. 朝ご飯 = breakfast. 夜ご飯 = dinner.
example_japanese: ご飯を 食べましょう！

japanese: アレルギーがあります
usage_note: アレルギー = allergy (from English). あります = there is / I have. Say the food before it.
example_japanese: えびアレルギーが あります。

japanese: 肉なしでお願いします
usage_note: 〜なしで = without ___. お願いします = please. Works for any ingredient — 魚なし = no fish.
example_japanese: 肉なしで お願いします。

japanese: お会計をお願いします
usage_note: お会計 = the bill/check. This is the polite standard way to ask for your check at a restaurant.
example_japanese: すみません、お会計を お願いします。

usage_note: Japanese counting for people is special: 一人 (hitori), 二人 (futari). From three: 三人 (sannin).
example_japanese: 二人 です。

usage_note: Japanese counting for people is special: 一人 (hitori), 二人 (futari). From three: 三人 (sannin).
example_japanese: 二人 です。

usage_note: 予約 = reservation/booking. あります = have/exists. ありません = don't have.
example_japanese: ジョンの名前で 予約があります。
example_english: I have a reservation under the name Jon.

usage_note: 食べます = eat. 飲みます = drink. Two of the most common verbs at any meal.
example_japanese: 一緒に 食べましょう！

usage_note: 食べます = eat. 飲みます = drink. Two of the most common verbs at any meal.
example_japanese: 一緒に 食べましょう！

english: How many? / How old are you?
usage_note: Context tells you which meaning. At a restaurant = how many people. In conversation = how old.
example_japanese: 何名様 ですか？

usage_note: The word for a Christian church building or congregation. You'll say this every day.
example_japanese: 教会に 来てください。

usage_note: 礼 = ceremony/bow. 拝 = worship. Together = a worship service or church service.
example_japanese: 今週の日曜日に 礼拝が あります。
example_english: There is a worship service this Sunday.

usage_note: 祈り = prayer (the noun). 祈ります = I pray (the verb). Both essential for ministry.
example_japanese: あなたのために 祈ります。

usage_note: 祈り = prayer (the noun). 祈ります = I pray (the verb). Both essential for ministry.
example_japanese: あなたのために 祈ります。

usage_note: 聖 = holy/sacred. 書 = book/writing. The Holy Scriptures.
example_japanese: 一緒に 聖書を 読みましょう。

usage_note: 神 = god/deity. 様 = honorific suffix (like Lord). Always use 神様 when referring to God respectfully.
example_japanese: 神様は あなたを 愛しています。

usage_note: イエス = Jesus (phonetic). 様 = honorific (Lord / respected person). Always add 様 for respect.
example_japanese: イエス様は 私たちのために 来ました。

usage_note: 信じる = to believe. 信じます = I believe (polite). 信じていますか？ = Do you believe?
example_japanese: イエス様を 信じます。

usage_note: 信 = trust/believe. 仰 = look up to. Together = faith — looking up in trust.
example_japanese: 私の信仰は 神様に あります。

usage_note: Borrowed from English. Easy to say and immediately understood by anyone in Japan.
example_japanese: 私は クリスチャン です。

usage_note: 洗 = wash/cleanse. 礼 = ceremony. The ceremony of washing — baptism.
example_japanese: 洗礼を 受けましたか？

usage_note: From 救う (sukuu) = to save/rescue. 救い = the act of saving — salvation.
example_japanese: イエス様は 私たちに 救いを 与えました。

usage_note: A beautiful word meaning grace, blessing, or gift from above. Often used in hymns and prayer.
example_japanese: 神様の恵みは 大きいです。

usage_note: The word for love — deep, unconditional love. 神様の愛 = God's love.
example_japanese: 神様の愛は 永遠です。

japanese: 神様はあなたを愛しています
romaji: kamisama wa anata o aishite imasu
usage_note: One of the most important sentences you'll say. 愛しています = is loving (ongoing, present).
example_japanese: 神様は あなたを 愛しています。本当に。

usage_note: 一緒に = together. 〜ましょう = let's do ___. A warm, inviting phrase.
example_japanese: 一緒に 祈りましょう。

english: Please come to the worship service
usage_note: 礼拝 = worship service. に = to (direction). 来てください = please come.
example_japanese: 今週の日曜日に 礼拝に 来てください。
example_english: Please come to the worship service this Sunday.

japanese: あなたのために祈ってもいいですか？
romaji: anata no tame ni inotte mo ii desu ka?
usage_note: 〜てもいいですか = is it okay if I...? Very polite. This phrase opens hearts.
example_japanese: あなたのために 祈ってもいいですか？

japanese: 神様の平和があなたと共にありますように
romaji: kamisama no heiwa ga anata to tomo ni arimasu you ni
english: May God's peace be with you
usage_note: 〜ように = may it be that... A blessing/wish. Beautiful farewell after prayer.
example_japanese: 神様の平和が あなたと共に ありますように。
example_english: May God's peace be with you.
literal_breakdown: God's peace [subject] → you with together → may it be.

usage_note: 賛 = praise. 美 = beauty. 歌 = song. A praise song or hymn sung in church.
example_japanese: 一緒に 賛美歌を 歌いましょう。

usage_note: 牧 = shepherd/tend. 師 = teacher/master. The shepherd-teacher — a pastor.
example_japanese: 牧師は どこにいますか？

usage_note: 宣 = proclaim. 教 = teach. 師 = master. One who proclaims and teaches — a missionary.
example_japanese: 私は アメリカからの 宣教師です。
example_english: I am a missionary from America.

usage_note: Your personal story of faith. 証しをしてもいいですか？ = May I share my testimony?
example_japanese: 私の証しを 聞いてください。

usage_note: 福 = blessing/fortune. 音 = sound/news. Literally 'good tidings' — the gospel.
example_japanese: これが イエス様の 福音です。
example_english: This is the gospel of Lord Jesus.

usage_note: 希 = rare/hope. 望 = wish/desire. Together = hope — a precious and rare desire.
example_japanese: イエス様は 私たちの 希望です。

usage_note: 平 = flat/peaceful. 和 = harmony/Japan. Together = peace and harmony.
example_japanese: 神様の平和が あなたと共に ありますように。
example_english: May God's peace be with you.
literal_breakdown: God's peace [subject] → with you → may it be.

usage_note: The deep, lasting joy that comes from faith. Different from happiness which depends on circumstances.
example_japanese: 神様の喜びが あなたの力です。
example_english: The joy of God is your strength.

usage_note: Deeper than ありがとう. Used in prayer or when you're truly moved with gratitude.
example_japanese: 神様に 感謝します。

japanese: 私はクリスチャンです
usage_note: Simple and clear. Your identity in one sentence. Say it confidently.
example_japanese: 私は クリスチャン です。アメリカの教会から来ました。
example_english: I am a Christian. I came from a church in America.
literal_breakdown: I [topic] → Christian → am. America's church [from] → came.

japanese: 日本のために祈っています
romaji: nihon no tame ni inotte imasu
usage_note: 〜のために = for the sake of. 〜ています = ongoing action. Powerful sentence for why you came.
example_japanese: アメリカから来ました。日本のために 祈っています。
example_english: I came from America. I am praying for Japan.

japanese: イエスは私たちのために死にました
romaji: Iesu wa watashitachi no tame ni shinimashita
usage_note: 私たち = we/us. 〜のために = for the sake of. 死にました = died (past polite).
example_japanese: イエス様は 私たちのために 死にました。

usage_note: でも = but/however. 復活 = resurrection. しました = did (past). The heart of the gospel.
example_japanese: 死にました。でも、復活しました！
example_english: He died. But he rose again!

usage_note: 罪 = sin/crime. の = possessive. 赦し = forgiveness/pardon. Core gospel vocabulary.
example_japanese: イエス様は 罪の赦しを 与えます。
example_english: Lord Jesus gives forgiveness of sins.

usage_note: 永遠 = eternal/forever. の = possessive. いのち = life. The promise of the gospel.
example_japanese: 信じれば 永遠のいのちを 得ます。
example_english: If you believe, you will receive eternal life.

english: If you believe, you will be saved
usage_note: 〜れば = if ___. 救われます = will be saved (passive polite). A key gospel statement.
example_japanese: イエス様を 信じれば 救われます。
example_english: If you believe in Lord Jesus, you will be saved.
literal_breakdown: Lord Jesus [object] → if believe → will be saved.

japanese: あなたのために祈ります
usage_note: あなたのために = for you / for your sake. 祈ります = I will pray. A parting gift of love.
example_japanese: あなたのために 祈ります。神様が 守ってくださいますように。
example_english: I will pray for you. May God protect you.
literal_breakdown: You [for] → will pray. God [subject] → may protect you.

japanese: 神様の祝福がありますように
romaji: Kamisama no shukufuku ga arimasu you ni
usage_note: 祝福 = blessing. 〜ように = may it be that... A blessing or wish for someone.
example_japanese: 神様の祝福が ありますように。またね。
literal_breakdown: God's blessing [subject] → may there be. Bye.
